title: Implement parse_subject() — multi-part subject line parser
description:
Implement the subject line parser in src/subject.rs.

Goal: given a raw email/Usenet Subject header value, extract the part number, total parts, and a normalized stem (filename or topic string) if present.

Public type:
  pub struct SubjectParts {
      pub part: u32,           // 1-based part number
      pub total: Option<u32>,  // None if not determinable from subject
      pub stem: Option<String>, // normalized title/filename portion, whitespace-trimmed
  }

Public function:
  pub fn parse_subject(subject: &str) -> Option<SubjectParts>
  // Returns None if no part marker can be found (single-part or unrelated message)

Patterns to handle (derived from MIME-zjr.1 research; update list after research completes):
  - '(03/17)' suffix: part=3, total=17
  - '[03/17]' variant
  - 'Part 3/17', 'Part 03 of 17', 'Part3of17' (case-insensitive)
  - '[BINARY] filename - Part 3 of 12'
  - 'filename.tar.gz - 03/17'
  - Part 0 (TOC): parse_subject returns SubjectParts { part: 0, total: Some(N), stem: ... }
  - Subject with no part marker: return None
  - yEnc marker '=yenc' in subject: return None (out of scope; document why)

Implementation approach: compiled regex via the 'regex' crate. Use a prioritized list of patterns tried in order (most specific first). Avoid catastrophic backtracking — no nested quantifiers over unbounded ranges.

Tests (oracle: real Usenet/email subject lines from public archives, NOT generated by this code):
  - Each pattern variant above, at least 2 examples each
  - Verify stem extraction is trimmed of surrounding punctuation
  - Part 0 parsed correctly
  - yEnc line returns None
  - Garbage string returns None
  - Unicode in stem (non-ASCII filename) — should not panic

PARENT: MIME-zjr
